budget.title: Monthly spending budget
budget.description: Set a limit once and your wallet signs only for that: the amount leaves your wallet into a program account the chain derives from your wallet — not to Payvand, not to the seller. Only your wallet can take it back out, while this device's session key spends from it inside the limit with no approval popups.

whereMoney.title: Where the money sits.
whereMoney.body: The pot is a program account derived from your wallet: setting or refilling a limit moves that amount out of your wallet and into it, and only your wallet can take it back out. This device's session key can spend from it, but never more than the limit. The limit resets on the 1st of each month, the pot keeps whatever you did not spend, and closing the budget returns every unit to your wallet.

keepSmall.title: Keep it small on purpose.
keepSmall.body: A limit you could lose without changing your month is doing its job — that is why payments from it never ask for an approval. Pair it with a wallet used only for spending, apart from savings:

foreign.title: This allowance is registered to another device
foreign.withKey: The key that pays silently here belongs to a different device ({key}). Taking it over needs one approval, moves no funds, and stops the other device from spending.
foreign.description: The key that pays silently for this allowance lives on another device. Taking it over needs one approval, moves no funds, and stops the other device from spending.

budget.limitHelp: Applied on the next signature — top up, lower, or raise it any time.
budget.lowLimitWarning: Any device holding your session key can pay up to this amount without asking your wallet, so it is also the most a stolen phone or laptop could spend. Start low and raise it whenever you need more.

killSwitch.title: Closing the budget is the kill switch.
killSwitch.body: It revokes the session key on every device, returns everything left to your wallet, and stops silent payments at once — then a new limit can be set whenever you are ready.

oneApproval.title: What this one approval does.
oneApproval.body: It moves the limit out of your wallet into a program account the chain derives from your wallet — not to Payvand, and not to the seller — and registers a session key that stays on this device. Payments inside the limit then go through with no popups, and only your wallet can withdraw the pot.

privacy.metaDescription: What Payvand stores, why it stores it, and what stays in your browser: an email and a hashed password, the shops and codes you create, and no tracking, no ads and no wallet keys.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What Payvand stores, why it stores it, and what never leaves your browser.

short.title: The short version
short.email: An account is an email address and a password. We keep the email and a one-way hash of the password — never the password itself.
short.keep: We keep what you create: shops, products, payment codes and discount codes.
short.noAds: No advertising, no analytics, no tracking pixels, and no selling or sharing your data for marketing. There is none of it in the app to switch off.
short.keys: Your wallet's keys never reach us, so we cannot move your money or read your balance without asking the network, as anyone can.
short.chain: Payments are recorded on a public blockchain: visible to anyone, permanently, and not deletable by us or by you.

store.title: What we store, and why
store.accountBody: The email address (to sign in and to reach you), a hash of your password made with Argon2, and the wallet address once you link one (so the app knows which shops, payments and discount codes are yours).
store.sessionsBody: A random token, kept hashed, with the time it was created and the time it expires. A session lasts 30 days; signing out deletes it.
store.createdBody: Shop names and descriptions, product names, details and prices, saved payment codes, and discount codes with their percentages.
store.resetsBody: A hashed token that works once and expires after an hour.
store.waitlistBody: The email address you submit, until it is used or removed.
store.logsBody: Errors are logged so the service can be fixed. The log does not contain passwords, and error messages shown to the app no longer contain database detail.

visible.title: What other people can see
visible.codeBody: It travels in a URL or a QR code and contains the seller's wallet address, the amount, a reference, the item name and the memo the seller typed. When the code was made while signed in, it also carries the seller's account id as a hint, so the checkout knows to offer that seller's discount codes. Anyone holding the code sees all of that.
visible.shopBody: Shops have a public link: the name, description, products and prices on it are readable by anyone with the link.
visible.chainBody: A payment writes the two wallet addresses, the amount and the time into a public ledger that anyone can read and nobody can edit.
visible.email: Your email address and password hash are not published anywhere and do not appear in a payment code.

keys.title: Wallet keys are not ours to hold
keys.real: Every real payment is approved inside your own wallet. Payvand never has the keys to it and cannot sign for it.
keys.budget: The practice budget is signed with a key your browser generates and keeps as a non-extractable browser key: it can sign while you use the app, but it cannot be read back out — not by this app, not by a script on the page. It never leaves your device, and we have no copy.
keys.never: We never ask for a seed phrase and never store private keys. There is nothing here for a thief to take but an email address and a hash.

browser.title: What is kept in your browser
browser.localBody: Your session token and a copy of your profile, so the header does not flicker while it loads; the currency you chose; the wallet you connected last; and your light or dark theme.
browser.indexedBody: The practice budget's key, in the form described above.
browser.cacheBody: It keeps the app's own files so it opens offline. It deliberately never caches payment pages or payment status, so you are never shown a stale amount.
browser.none: There are no advertising or analytics cookies. Clearing this site's data signs you out on that device and forgets those choices.

others.title: Who else is involved
others.hosting: A hosting provider runs the website and the API.
others.db: A hosted SQL database (libSQL) stores the accounts, shops and codes.
others.solana: The Solana network, reached through an RPC provider, is read for balances and payment status. Payments themselves are sent by your wallet, not by us.
others.email: An email provider delivers the few messages the app sends: sign-in notices, password resets, and a note if someone tries to sign up with your address.
others.body: These providers handle the data only to run the service for us. We do not sell it, we do not share it for advertising, and there is no analytics network watching these pages.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.account: Your account and everything you create: until the account is deleted.
retention.sessions: Sessions: 30 days, then expired and swept away.
retention.waitlist: Waiting list entries: until the invitation is used or the address is removed.
retention.logs: Server logs: as long as the hosting provider keeps them, usually days to weeks.
retention.chain: Anything written to the Solana blockchain: forever. Nobody can delete it, including us.

deletion.title: Deleting your data
deletion.body: Ask us and we will remove the account: its email, password hash, linked wallet, shops, products, saved payment codes, discount codes, sessions and any pending reset link. Deleting the account does not, and cannot, remove payments already recorded on the blockchain — that history belongs to the network, not to us. There is no self-service delete button yet, so a person does it.

children.title: Children
children.body: Payvand is not for anyone under 13, or under the age at which you can agree to the terms where you live. We do not knowingly keep an account for a child; if you think one exists, tell us and we will remove it.

changes.title: Changes, and contact
changes.body: If what the app stores changes, this page changes with it and the date at the bottom moves.
changes.contact: Questions about your data, or a deletion request: reply to any email Payvand has sent you. The address it came from reaches whoever runs this.

terms.metaDescription: What Payvand does, what it does not do, and the handful of rules that come with using it: payments go wallet to wallet, we never hold the money, and a paid transaction cannot be taken back.
terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: What Payvand does, what it does not do, and the handful of rules that come with using it.

what.title: What Payvand is
what.body: Payvand turns an amount into a payment code. A seller types in what something costs, the app builds a QR code, and a customer scans it with a Solana wallet and approves one transaction. The money moves from the customer's wallet to the seller's wallet over the Solana network — there is no account in the middle and no card processor.
what.accept: Using the app means you accept these terms. If you do not, please do not use it.

money.title: We never hold the money
money.hold: Payvand does not hold, receive or pass on your funds at any point, and has no way to move, freeze or take them.
money.reverse: We cannot cancel, reverse or refund a payment. Only the recipient can send money back, from their own wallet.
money.seed: We never ask for a seed phrase or a private key, and nobody working on Payvand will ever ask you for one. Anyone who does is not us.
money.budgetBefore: The only thing the app can sign without your wallet is the practice budget, with a key your own browser creates and keeps (see the

account.title: Your account
account.email: An account is an email address and a password. The password is stored as a one-way hash, never as the password itself.
account.password: Keep the password to yourself. What happens under your account is your responsibility, so tell us if you think someone else has it.
account.wallet: Link a wallet address you actually control: that link is how the app recognises your shops, your payments and your discount codes.
account.close: You can close your account by asking us (see Contact). Removing an account also removes its shops, products, payment codes, discount codes and sessions.
account.age: You must be old enough to agree to these terms where you live, and at least 13.

selling.title: If you are selling
selling.record: You are the seller of record. Prices, descriptions, taxes, receipts, refunds and consumer law are yours to get right, not ours.
selling.final: A payment that lands is final. If you want to give money back, send it back from your wallet — we cannot do it for you.
selling.public: What you publish is public. A payment code carries your wallet address, the amount, a reference, and the item name and memo you typed. Do not put anything private in those fields.
selling.law: Do not sell anything you are not allowed to sell where you are, and do not use Payvand for fraud, money laundering or to get around sanctions.

paying.title: If you are paying
paying.read: Read the amount and the address your wallet shows before you approve. The wallet is the last place anything can be checked, and it is telling you the truth.
paying.undo: A confirmed payment cannot be undone by us, by the app, or by the seller's goodwill alone.
paying.fiat: A price shown in your own currency is an indicative conversion at a market rate, not a quote from us, and the network settles in SOL.
paying.trust: Only pay codes from sellers you trust. A QR code is just data: anyone can print it, edit it or send you one.

fees.title: Fees
fees.body: Payvand charges nothing for making or scanning a payment code. The Solana network charges a small fee for the transaction, and a payment creates a record on chain that costs a little rent — both are paid from the customer's wallet, and the wallet shows the total before you approve anything.

testMoney.title: Test money
testMoney.before: When the badge in the corner says
testMoney.after: , the app is running on Solana's test network and the SOL involved is not worth anything. It is there so you can practise. It is not a promise that real money behaves the same way, and nothing on devnet has value.

fairUse.title: Fair use
fairUse.body: Do not attack the service or work around its limits: no scanning for weaknesses without asking first, no automated guessing of passwords or discount codes, no scraping, no hammering the API. We may suspend or remove an account that does any of that, and we may report it.

availability.title: Availability, and what we do not promise
availability.asIs: Payvand is provided as it is. We do not promise it will be available, that it will not lose data, or that it will keep working the same way — it may change or be discontinued.
availability.advice: Nothing here is financial, investment, tax or legal advice.
availability.liability: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, for a payment you approved in your wallet, or for what a seller does or sells. Our total liability is limited to what you have paid us to use Payvand, which is nothing.
availability.limits: Some places do not allow limits like these. Where that is the case, they apply only as far as the law there allows.

changes.title: Changes, and contact
changes.body: We will update this page when the app changes, and change the date at the bottom. Using Payvand after a change means you accept the new version.
changes.contact: Questions about these terms: reply to any email Payvand has sent you. The address it came from reaches whoever runs this.

terms.footer: Last updated {date}. This page is written to describe what the software actually does, in plain words.

wallet.none: No wallet detected. Install a Solana wallet extension and reload.

waitlist.title: This is a test build
waitlist.body: Payvand is a proof of concept. Codes, scanning and receipts all work, but every payment runs on a Solana test network with free test SOL — no real money moves.
waitlist.invite: Want to take real payments? Leave your email and we'll tell you when Payvand is ready for a live wallet.
waitlist.joinFailure: Could not add you to the list. Try again in a moment.
waitlist.successBody: We'll email you when Payvand can take real payments.
